tasks.short: Plan flight activities and test schedules and prepare flight evaluation reports.

steps.what: Define flight-test objectives, operating limits, measurements and evaluation criteria
Draft the test schedule from confirmed aircraft, crew and airfield availability
outputs: candidate flight activity and test schedule

steps.what: Check and approve the complete flight activities, test schedule and crew instructions
inputs: candidate flight activity and test schedule

steps.what: Send the approved test activity package to the internal test crew
Verify returned flight-test data, flown conditions and deviations against the approved plan
Populate factual flight evaluation tables using the verified test dataset
Prepare the flight evaluation report's interpretation, limitations and conclusions
Approve the final complete report, evidence references and internal audience
File the approved flight evaluation report
Send the approved report link to the internal evaluation team

tasks.design: Keep flight-test design, final activity approval, returned-data verification and evaluation conclusions human. Use native {CALENDAR}/{SPREADSHEET} resource checks first, with a deterministic scheduler only if needed, and populate exact factual report tables in {DOCS}. {OTHER} is the operator's authorised test-data viewer. Activity delivery, report filing and report delivery are distinct actions gated on their respective completed versions.
tasks.previous_blocker: A planned test, an actually flown test and a defensible evaluation are different artefacts.
tasks.enabler_now: Explicit availability and verified numeric test records can support scheduling and factual report assembly.
tasks.still_hard: Safe test design, interpreting deviations and deciding what results establish remain expert work.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when an apparently good result was obtained under conditions that invalidate the intended test.
tasks.altitude: Less schedule comparison and factual table preparation; unchanged flight evaluation judgement.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: explicit resource constraints and verified test datasets can support deterministic scheduling and factual tables without deciding flight safety.

assumptions: Provisional shares concern planning and evaluation work, including report preparation and sends. Flight execution itself is a separate operational task; its labour is not claimed as saved. Existing schedule/table automation gives no new benefit.

s1 pilot supplies test_id, objective, sequence, duration, limits, measurement, unit and acceptance_criterion, and confirms/captures aircraft_id, crew_id, resource_window and airfield_constraint from operations. All original input capture and missing-source resolution stay fully counted there.

After s4, the authorised flight-test crew produces returned records with test_id, aircraft_id, actual_conditions, timestamp, measurement, value, unit, source_reference and deviation. s5 retains all match, completeness and factual validation; missing or noncomparable data are investigated manually. No data is available merely because the test was scheduled.

s6 copies verified values and prespecified comparisons only; s7 retains interpretation, uncertainty and conclusions. Native export/report templates are tried first, without inventing a new clean dataset.

a1 binds the actual final activity instructions and crew recipients after s3. a2/a3 bind the actual final report hash, access and audience after s8. Changes revoke the respective approval. No flight authorisation or external regulatory submission is automated.
research_questions: Which manual schedule and table operations remain once actual source capture and verification are counted?

incremental.description: Maintain resource constraints and test-to-report mapping

approvals.approved_version: s3 final activity/test package and internal crew recipients
s8 complete final report and storage access
s8 final report hash and internal evaluation recipients

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves 10 schedule, 10 factual table and 7 send/file hours minus 1 upkeep = 26. Low halves schedule benefit and retains other actions: 5 minus 1 = 4. Test design, input capture and report conclusions retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Teach company regulations and procedures to other pilots.

steps.what: Select current company procedure revisions and identify the pilots' training needs
Prepare and check the final procedure handout using approved manual extracts
Teach company regulations and procedures and explain their operational application
Work through operational scenarios and check pilots' understanding of the procedure
Write and approve the actual attendance, training outcome and follow-up record
Commit the approved completed-training record to the learning system

tasks.design: Use a native {DOCS} teaching template that references exact approved manual extracts and revision identifiers. Keep source selection, final material checks, instruction and scenario assessment human. Record actual completion after teaching; a separate native {LMS} commit follows approval of that completed record. No model paraphrases mandatory procedures or marks completion from enrolment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedure currency and pilots' practical understanding matter more than distributing text.
tasks.enabler_now: Native linked extracts and templates can reduce repeated handout formatting without changing approved wording.
tasks.still_hard: Explaining operational exceptions and recognising misunderstanding require an instructor.
tasks.human_edge: Connect a company rule to a realistic flight situation and probe unsafe assumptions.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated material formatting and completion-record transfer.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native document templates can reuse exact approved procedure extracts and learning systems can file checked completion records.

assumptions: Shares are provisional for instructor work. Actual manual handout-formatting and record-transfer steps need observation; existing native reuse/save earns no additional benefit.

Manual owner supplies procedure_id, revision, effective_date and approved_text. s1 instructor confirms scope and captures section references; s2 retains 9 hours for choosing examples, assembling variable content and checking actual final material. Missing/currentness issues are resolved manually before teaching.

s5 instructor captures pilot_id, session_id, procedure_revision, actual_attendance, observed_outcome and follow_up after s4. Original capture/checking remains full time; no attendance or completion feed is invented.

a1 binds the actual completed-training record and learner IDs after s5; edits revoke approval. No pretraining notices or enrolment actions are introduced or confused with completion. Teaching materials are instructor aids here, with no separate automated distribution claim.
research_questions: Can native extracts retain exact current wording and remove manual formatting without reducing preparation checks?

incremental.description: Check manual revision links and learning-record mapping

approvals.approved_version: s5 final actual attendance/outcome record and pilot IDs

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central saves 6 handout-formatting and 2 record-commit hours minus 0.5 upkeep = 7.5. Low halves only formatting benefit and keeps save manual: 3 minus 0.5 = 2.5. Teaching, scenarios and actual outcome capture retain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Keep flight-test and instruction judgement with the pilot while improving exact planning and record operations.
reach: Help test and training teams distinguish approved plans from actual execution and completed evaluation.
role.ambitious_version: A pilot whose test reports and training records reflect what actually happened, supported by reliable native document tools.
